title: Rigveda 1.179: Lopamudra and Agastya
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.179: Lopamudra and Agastya: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.179 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agastya and Lopamudra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 140r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.

Gaps: verses 1.179.3, 1.179.4 were rendered by Griffith in Latin, not English, and are not shown.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.179.1-6 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 4, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 140r
translation.original_text:
1pū̱rvīr a̱haṁ śa̱rada̍ḥ śaśramā̱ṇā do̱ṣā vasto̍r u̱ṣaso̍ ja̱raya̍ntīḥ | mi̱nāti̱ śriya̍ṁ jari̱mā ta̱nūnā̱m apy ū̱ nu patnī̱r vṛṣa̍ṇo jagamyuḥ ||
2ye ci̱d dhi pūrva̍ ṛta̱sāpa̱ āsa̍n sā̱kaṁ de̱vebhi̱r ava̍dann ṛ̱tāni̍ | te ci̱d avā̍sur na̱hy anta̍m ā̱puḥ sam ū̱ nu patnī̱r vṛṣa̍bhir jagamyuḥ ||
5i̱maṁ nu soma̱m anti̍to hṛ̱tsu pī̱tam upa̍ bruve | yat sī̱m āga̍ś cakṛ̱mā tat su mṛ̍ḻatu pulu̱kāmo̱ hi martya̍ḥ ||
6a̱gastya̱ḥ khana̍mānaḥ kha̱nitrai̍ḥ pra̱jām apa̍tya̱m bala̍m i̱cchamā̍naḥ | u̱bhau varṇā̱v ṛṣi̍r u̱graḥ pu̍poṣa sa̱tyā de̱veṣv ā̱śiṣo̍ jagāma ||
translation.text:
1'Through many autumns have I toiled and laboured, at night and morn, through age-inducing dawnings. Old age impairs the beauty of our bodies. Let husbands still come near unto their spouses.
2For even the men aforetime, law-fulfillers, who with the Gods declared eternal statutes,– – They have decided, but have not accomplished: so now let wives come near unto their husbands.
5This Soma I address that is most near us, that which hath been imbibed within the spirit, To pardon any sins we have committed. Verily mortal man is full of longings.
6Agastya thus, toiling with strong endeavour, wishing for children, progeny and power, Cherished – a sage of mighty strength – both classes, and with the Gods obtained his prayer's fulfilment.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 140r (numbered 9r by the scribe) (OPenn image 141, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.178.5 ‹-manyamānān tvam trātā tvam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 140v (numbered 9v by the scribe), begins in RV 1.180.1 ‹-dīyat hiraṇyayā vām pavayaḥ›. Verses 1.179.1-6 end on this page.

2ye | cit | hi | pūrve | ṛta-sāpaḥ | āsan | sākam | devebhiḥ | avadan | ṛtāni | te | cit | ava | asuḥ | nahi | antam | āpuḥ | sam | oṃ iti | nu | patnīḥ | vṛṣa-bhiḥ | jagamyuḥ
